preamble: In Northern Berber languages the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ] (written ⟨ɣ⟩) has no geminate of its own: whenever it is geminated, typically in the imperfective (intensive) stem of verbs, it surfaces as the voiceless uvular stop [qː]. Gemination thus brings fortition and devoicing together, alongside the parallel alternations w ~ bb/ggʷ and y ~ gg. The pattern is synchronic and morphophonemic. Proto-Berber reconstructions already pair singleton *ɣ with geminate *qq, so it is not a recent diachronic change. It is described for Tashelhit (Shilha), among others.

examples.to: aqqra [aqːra] (imperfective), as in ar yaqqra 'he is reading'
examples.note: Under morphological gemination ɣɣ is realized as qq and labialized ɣɣ° as qq°.
Same imperfective gemination; the derived agent noun amqqrs 'slaughterer' also has qq.
